lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, no coloured vessels and median test results), the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about {{C03.risk.from|pct}}.
The model adds up six parts, one of them a weighted sum of most inputs.

sentences.text: These inputs add up independently, biggest first: more vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raise the predicted risk steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same, from about {{C25.risk.from|pct}} at {{C25.statement.change.from}} to about {{C25.risk.to|pct}} at {{C25.statement.change.to}} for a typical patient, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.

A flat rather than an upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it from about {{C26.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C26.risk.to|pct}}, and higher cholesterol raises it steadily, from about {{C27.risk.from|pct}} at {{C27.statement.change.from}} to about {{C27.risk.to|pct}} at {{C27.statement.change.to}}.
Higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily, from about {{C28.risk.from|pct}} at {{C28.statement.change.from}} to about {{C28.risk.to|pct}} at {{C28.statement.change.to}}.

Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain (rather than no chest pain symptoms) and being a woman lower it from about {{C30.risk.from|pct}} to {{C30.risk.to|pct}}, about {{C33.risk.to|pct}} and about {{C32.risk.to|pct}} respectively; sex, chest pain type, fasting blood sugar, the thallium result and the vessel count also act through the parts below.

ST depression on exercise adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about {{C40.statement.threshold}} (checked for all {{C40.statement.support_check.n}} training patients): for a typical patient, going from {{C40.statement.change.from}} to {{C40.statement.change.to}} moves it from about {{C40.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C40.risk.to|pct}}.
This part acts on {{C41.statement.n_active}} of {{C41.statement.n}} patients, those past that point; {{C41.statement.outcome_in_group.positives}} of them had heart disease.

Being a woman rather than a man lowers the predicted risk, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: for a typical patient, from about {{C45.statement.stronger_group.risk_from|pct}} to {{C45.statement.stronger_group.risk_to|pct}} without chest pain on exercise, and from about {{C45.statement.weaker_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C45.statement.weaker_group.risk_to|pct}} with it.
This part acts on {{C46.statement.n_active}} of {{C46.statement.n}} patients, those without chest pain on exercise; {{C46.statement.outcome_in_group.positives}} of them had heart disease.
Through this part, chest pain brought on by exercise raises the predicted risk from about {{C44.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C44.risk.to|pct}} for a typical patient.

A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the predicted risk, but only if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less (checked for all {{C50.statement.support_check.n}} training patients with higher fasting blood sugar): for a typical patient, from about {{C50.statement.stronger_group.risk_from|pct}} to about {{C50.statement.stronger_group.risk_to|pct}} (the model has little data on this, n = {{C50.groups[2].n|d}}).
This part acts on {{C51.statement.n_active}} of {{C51.statement.n}} patients, those with a fixed defect; {{C51.statement.outcome_in_group.positives}} of them had heart disease.
For a typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is {{C51.risk.from|pct}} without this part and about {{C51.risk.to|pct}} with it (the model has little data on this, n = {{C51.groups[0].n|d}}).

Through this part, more coloured vessels raise the predicted risk a second time, steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, from about {{C54.risk.from|pct}} at {{C54.statement.change.from}} to about {{C54.risk.to|pct}} at {{C54.statement.change.to}}.

A thallium result the data does not decode ({{C53.groups[1].label}}) raises it from about {{C53.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C53.risk.to|pct}} (the model has little data on this, n = {{C53.groups[1].n|d}}).
This part flags atypical angina and barely changes the predictions, by at most {{C58.statement.max_change_in_risk|pct}}.
For a typical patient, atypical angina through this part moves the predicted risk from about {{C56.risk.from|pct}} to about {{C56.risk.to|pct}}.
